mutant.description: A mutant root outside every worktree holding copies of the record, both raw extracts and the check, with the BASELINE run there first and reading PASS on all three. Three mutants, one per criterion: (1) cause.claim set to 'probably', a value outside the ratified enum; (2) last_ready.at_utc set to null while claim stayed 'measured', the specific contradiction AC2 names; (3) a forbidden command appended to host_commands, 'systemctl restart irpt-analysis-resident.service'.
mutant.expected: AC1 FAIL on (1), AC2 FAIL on (2), AC3 FAIL on (3)
mutant.observed: (1) FAIL: cause needs statement, claim in ('measured','inferred','held','absent') and evidence_lines | AC1 FAIL rc=1. (2) FAIL: a null last READY cannot be measured; it is absent within the window | AC2 FAIL rc=1. (3) FAIL: host command mutant-0001 matches the forbidden pattern systemctl\s+(start|stop|restart|reload|enable|disable|kill) | AC3 FAIL rc=1. Each was reverted and all three re-read PASS. SEPARATELY, AND STRONGER THAN A PLANTED MUTANT: AC3's discrimination was demonstrated by the WORLD rather than by a copy -- it genuinely failed on the real record before AMENDMENT 1, and the amendment was then controlled in both directions (see determinism).

determinism.method: The amendment that unblocked AC3 was controlled rather than accepted: both repaired patterns were exercised against cases that must still match and cases that must not, to establish the fix NARROWED the check without blinding it. Separately, the diagnosis itself rests on bytes whose identity was checked: the host's run-ycharts-session.sh and ycharts_session.js were hashed on the instance and compared with the repository's at box/dell2 HEAD.
determinism.observed: 10 of 10 control cases correct. Runner pattern: still matches 'bash .../run-ycharts-session.sh', 'node .../ycharts_session.js' and 'sh .../ycharts_session.js'; no longer matches 'sha256sum a.sh b.js' or 'stat a.sh b.js'. Redirect pattern: still matches 'echo hi > /opt/x/file' and 'cat a >> /var/log/b'; no longer matches '2>/dev/null', a sed replacement containing >/I, or 'wc -l < /opt/x/f'. Host bytes: 55ddb8f7947cba7c and 857d90b81960d69a7a both EQUAL the repo, so the code quoted in the cause is the code that ran.

declared_exclusions.item: Any sign-in attempt, any run of run-ycharts-session.sh or ycharts_session.js, and any vendor call
declared_exclusions.reason: The order's HARD BOUNDS forbid them and the whole point of the cell is that the path is stopped. None was made: the record carries sign_in_attempted false and vendor_calls_made 0 with the evidence, and the journal shows no capture attempt after 11:19:20Z, before this read began at 12:54:41Z.

declared_exclusions.item: Any secret VALUE, including the YCharts login and session bundles
declared_exclusions.reason: Forbidden; get-secret-value was never invoked. Only describe-secret (dates and version stages) was used, and only the secret NAMES were read from secret-ids.env, which is what that file holds. secret_values_read is 0.

declared_exclusions.item: Starting, stopping or restarting the resident unit, touching the queue, or any write on the host
declared_exclusions.reason: Forbidden. systemctl was used only with `show`. No redirection to a host path, no temp file and no tee: the reads are one journalctl pass piped into one grep or awk per command, plus stat, wc, grep, find, sha256sum and two read-only get-items.

declared_exclusions.item: Driving a caller the function ADMITS, to see what a real request now gets
declared_exclusions.reason: Outside this cell: it would be a sign-in and a vendor call. It is also impossible from this seat, which cannot mint a verified internal subject -- the same ceiling 0.9.0_WK_IRPT_BCKEND~281 met.

declared_exclusions.item: The current values of capture_not_before and intent_session_refresh
declared_exclusions.reason: Both live on rows not locatable without a table scan, which is outside the describe-and-listing read shape the order sanctions. Where each is stored, when it is set and what clears it are read from the code instead, and the cooldown's 900 s EFFECT is measured five times from journal spacing.
